metadata.title: Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations and Sharp Interpolation Estimates

sections.heading: Claims
sections.text:
Solves the sharp-constant variational problem for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg interpolation inequality in the
L2-critical case (nonlinearity power σ = 2/N), and shows the best constant is attained exactly at the
ground-state (Townes) solitary-wave profile. This gives a rigorous, sharp threshold — not just an upper or
lower bound — for global existence vs. blow-up in the critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation: solutions
with power (L² norm) below the Townes profile's own power exist for all time, and the threshold is exactly
p_cr ≈ 1.86 in this normalization (the 2D cubic case, N=2, σ=1, is the critical case the project's own
Request 4 comparison targets — see [[RESEARCH FINDINGS - Quantule Mapper Discriminating Evidence]]).
